title: The Streak (professional wrestling)
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of "The Streak," The Undertaker's (Mark Calaway) historic series of 21 consecutive victories at WWE's flagship event, WrestleMania, spanning from his win over Jimmy Snuka at WrestleMania VII in 1991 until his final win against CM Punk at WrestleMania 29 in 2013. The document begins with background information on WrestleMania's significance as WWE's premier annual event and The Undertaker's career history, including his championship accomplishments. It then presents a detailed chronological account of the Streak's progression, organized by milestone stages: the beginning wins (4–0) against opponents like Jimmy Snuka, Jake "The Snake" Roberts, Giant Gonzáles, and King Kong Bundy; major feuds (8–0) with Diesel, Sycho Sid, Kane, and Big Boss Man; the "American Bad-Ass" era (11–0) featuring Triple H and Ric Flair; the Streak defense period (14–0) against Kane, Randy Orton, and Mark Henry; championship pursuits (16–0) against Batista and Edge; the acclaimed two-match rivalry with Shawn Michaels (18–0); and final wins (21–0) against Triple H and CM Punk. Each match account includes storylines, key moments, finishing maneuvers, and behind-the-scenes insights from interviews. The document also covers the controversial end of the Streak at WrestleMania XXX in 2014, when Brock Lesnar defeated The Undertaker, detailing the shocking crowd reaction, the decision-making process behind ending the Streak, and its aftermath—including The Undertaker's subsequent WrestleMania matches and final record of 25–2. Additional sections address reactions and legacy from fellow wrestlers, media coverage through WWE DVDs, and the Streak's inclusion in video games such as WWE SmackDown vs. Raw 2011 and WWE 2K14.
